prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I keep B011 as a single-part prize with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. After round 1 it is the only item preferred by more than one member (four of eight), and all eight files carry it in a preferred configuration or alternatives list, so the disagreement is about maturity and credit and not about the mechanism. The physical content is what I weigh most: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex with a target and an E3 ligase, the cooperativity of that complex is measurable and predictive, and the outcome is elimination of the protein rather than occupancy. That is a new capability and has been reproduced across many laboratories and target classes. I would answer the chair's own question on maturity as follows: the citation should rest on the chemical principle and the design rules that make it general, which is established, and should not claim therapeutic success. If a degrader were approved by announcement that would strengthen the case, but I would not make my vote depend on it.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, and I cannot verify current trial outcomes, so the prize may look early. Three names leave out Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper and the molecular-glue strand of Handa, Ito and Gray. The citation has to be worded as a statement about recruiting E3 ligases with small molecules by design, and the committee has to say openly that the cereblon and thalidomide mechanism is a related but separate achievement that can be recognised later. If the committee is not willing to defend that omission, B011 is weaker than its support count suggests.

responses.point: Chabes keeps B011 first but replaces Ciulli with Handa, and words the citation to run from PROTACs to the molecular basis of thalidomide-class glues.
responses.response: I have thought about this again and I still hold Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Handa's identification of cereblon is a clear mechanistic discovery, but it explains why existing drugs work. The PROTAC concept plus structure-guided ternary-complex design is what turns degradation into something chemists can do on demand for a chosen target. A citation that tries to cover both strands with three names has to omit either Ciulli or Ito and Gray, and a broader wording invites a priority dispute. I would accept Handa only if Andrei can show that the PROTAC strand could not stand without the glue discovery. Otherwise I think we agree on the prize and differ on how much the citation should say.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps Gray and Winkler (B058) first as a mature, physically stated mechanism, and presses on the narrowness of any citation relative to Marcus, Hopfield, Dutton and Moser.
responses.response: Peter answered my round-1 question by narrowing the claim to the experimental demonstration in proteins with ruthenium-modified systems, and that is a fair statement. It makes B058 a defensible and mature item, and I put it among my alternatives for that reason. It still does not move ahead of B011 for me, because the citation would sit next to Marcus's 1992 theory prize and next to the Dutton and Moser distance relation. The strength of the case is confirmation of a principle that is already largely accepted, while B011 provides a new capability. I would be comfortable with B058 as a fallback if B011 fails on attribution.

responses.point: Sparr keeps phase separation (B035) first, separating the established multivalency and demixing physics from over-extended in-cell claims, and lists B011 as her first alternative.
responses.response: The distinction between the polymer-physics core and the in-cell claims is useful, and it is the better argument for B035. As chair I still need a citation that does not claim more than the evidence supports, and a prize on the core alone would be awarded for an in vitro principle while the cell-biological meaning is disputed. Pappu and Mittag are central to that core and cannot be named within three names. Emma, since you list B011 as an alternative, I would ask whether you would move to it if B035 cannot reach five votes, and I would value that answer over the support count itself.

responses.point: Somfai holds Buchwald and Hartwig on Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B055) as a mature method used daily, acknowledges the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi precedent, and lists B011 as an alternative.
responses.response: I agree that adoption and thirty years of confirmation leave no doubt about maturity. My difficulty is the one Peter states himself: the committee already honoured Pd cross-coupling in 2010, and the C-N case would be read as an extension of a recognised field, with Kosugi's tin-amide precedent unresolved. Because only two members ranked B055 in their opening ballots, a vote for it would probably fail. I would like to hear whether he would accept B011 as a single-part prize, since his own file names it as an alternative.

responses.point: Aqvist holds B011 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, calls it a game-changer with a simple new principle, and concedes that it may be slightly early and that Sakamoto and Kim cannot be recognised under the cap.
responses.response: I agree with the principle and with Johan's reading of Ciulli's role: the structure-based design rules are the part that a physicist and a theorist find most convincing. On timing, I think the answer to the chair's question is that we hold B011 if the citation is drawn on chemistry, not on clinical results. I accept his point that omitting Sakamoto and Kim will have to be defended openly, and I would put that in the committee's reasoning rather than hide it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that the citation covers the PROTAC strand only and that the molecular-glue strand with Handa, Ito and Gray is left for a later prize.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader will cost B011 votes from members who weigh clinical validation, which I cannot verify.
Whether members with other first choices (Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr, Zou) will move to B011, and if they do not, whether any of B005, B058 or B035 can reach five votes.
I have not verified the living status of some credited individuals across ballots.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I share a Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr, and treat their views as ordinary colleague input. B017 (nanopores) is near my own field of nanofabricated devices, so I no longer carry it as a preferred or alternative item. As chair I will not let my own position count as more than one vote.
